claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II crew is returning from a 10-day moon mission.
The Artemis II crew will begin final reentry procedures around 7:33 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II crew module separates from the service module at 7:33 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II entry into Earth's atmosphere occurs at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II entry into Earth's atmosphere occurs at approximately 400,000 feet.
Artemis II drogue parachutes deploy at 8:03 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II drogue parachutes deploy at approximately 22,000 feet.
Artemis II main parachutes deploy at 8:04 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II main parachutes deploy at approximately 6,000 feet.
NASA and U.S. Navy teams will recover the Artemis II crew and the capsule following splashdown.
